title: Stacey Ryan
subtitle: Artist website redesign
intro: Stacey Ryan has <mark>1.6 million monthly listeners</mark>, <mark>over 500 million streams</mark> and a performance on <mark>The Late Late Show with James Corden</mark> behind her, but her website felt generic. With her debut album coming in 2025, she needed a site that felt like the record: old Hollywood glamour with traces of heartbreak. As the agency's <mark>sole designer</mark>, I designed it end to end and <mark>built much of it in Framer</mark>.
impact: <mark>Tripled ticket click-throughs</mark> compared to her previous shows, beating our goal of doubling them

blocks.html: Her brand booklet set the look: close-up portraits, Stacey as a <mark>vintage starlet in the Los Angeles desert</mark>, and bold, narrow fonts.

blocks.html: Sell the tour, not just the album

At the first client review, the focus moved from album presaves to Stacey's <mark>first headlining tour</mark>. With no target from the client, we set our own: <mark>double the ticket click-throughs</mark>.
I liked the old site's simplicity, but it was easy to see why Stacey wanted a change:

notes.text: a placeholder logo
social media links, barely visible
a generic headshot
yellow titles on white, hard to read
song titles disconnected from their cover art
music and video pages: generic grids
once again, a weird circle in the back
no set color palette, so no real identity
the tour, buried at the bottom, with room for only a few dates

blocks.text: Who is Stacey Ryan, and what is she trying to say? The old site never made that clear.

blocks.html: Keep the structure, change everything else
Most artist sites lead with the store. <mark>Benson Boone's</mark> came closest to what Stacey's team wanted:

notes.text: the same structure as Stacey's: music, videos, tour
a countdown to the album, which I used in my first version
presave and pre-order first
but the design felt dated
lots of shows, each with its own ticket link

blocks.html: My first direction was a <mark>summery, old-California look</mark>. Our team found it too summery, so instead of polishing it, I listened to the <mark>unreleased album</mark> to find her real vision.

blocks.html: Approved at the first client review
The client approved my first version with one change, for the new goal: <mark>move the tour to the top</mark>.
In the month after the tour announcement, <mark>ticket click-throughs tripled</mark> compared to her previous shows, beating our goal of doubling them.

blocks.text: The visuals were stunning, and the entire flow just worked. Fans love it, and so do I.

blocks.label: Walkthrough of the launched Stacey Ryan website

blocks.html: Design for where the audience actually is. After launch, analytics showed over 90% of visits came from phones. We made sure the site looked great on mobile, but I researched artist sites and designed on desktop first. Next time I'd check the data up front and start with mobile.
Immerse yourself in the material first. Listening to the unreleased album is what unlocked the right direction, not more research.
Learn the tool the design ships in. I learned Framer and built much of the site myself, which kept the launched version true to the design.
